Record what a mesh's coordinates mean

Source: R/mesh_space.R
mesh_space.Rd

A surface mesh on its own is just numbers: nothing in vertices says which hemisphere it is, which vertex space an atlas must have been built against to index it, or how to get from its coordinates to a standard space. Without that, consumers infer those things, and a mesh inferred wrongly still renders perfectly – a brain mirrored left-to-right, or regions painted at the wrong vertices, looks like a brain. mesh_space() makes the mesh state them.

Usage

mesh_space(
  vertex_space,
  hemi,
  anatomical,
  to_mni305 = NULL,
  units = "mm",
  surface = NULL,
  source = NULL
)

Arguments

vertex_space

Vertex space the mesh is in, such as "fsaverage5". Atlas vertex indices are only meaningful against a named space.

hemi

"left", "right" or "midline".

anatomical

Whether the coordinates correspond to positions in a brain. FALSE for inflated and spherical surfaces.

to_mni305

A 4x4 matrix mapping vertex coordinates to MNI305, or NULL when anatomical is FALSE.

units

Coordinate units. Millimetres throughout the ecosystem.

surface

Optional surface name, such as "pial".

source

Optional free-text note on where the mesh came from, for reproducibility. Never read by code; atlas_provenance() remains the authoritative record.

Value

A mesh_space object, to be attached with set_mesh_space().

Details

vertex_space is the mesh's identity as far as atlases are concerned. Atlases key regions to vertex indices, so an atlas built against one vertex space and drawn on another puts every region somewhere else. Checking that indices merely fit catches only the case where the other mesh is smaller.

Name a numbered space – "fsaverage5", "fsaverage6" – because those are fixed templates and stable across FreeSurfer releases: fsaverage5 is vertex-for-vertex the same mesh in 7.4.1 and 8.2.0, which is what makes an atlas's indices portable. Unnumbered "fsaverage" is not a stable identifier: it is whichever densest mesh that release ships, so the same string can mean different vertex counts and different indices. Record source if you must use it.

hemi is recorded because left and right are the one distinction this ecosystem must never get wrong, and a mesh that cannot state its own side cannot be checked against the data drawn on it.

to_mni305 is a 4x4 affine mapping the mesh's own vertex coordinates to MNI305, collapsing any axis permutation, sign flip and translation into one matrix. It is required when anatomical is TRUE and must be NULL otherwise: inflation and spherical registration move every vertex, so those surfaces have no anatomical position to map to and a matrix for them would be a number that looks usable.

Positioning a mesh for display – moving a hemisphere to meet the midline, say – is the renderer's decision, not a property of the mesh, so it is deliberately not recorded here.

See also

Other mesh spaces: brain_mesh(), set_mesh_space()

Examples

mesh_space(
  vertex_space = "fsaverage5",
  hemi = "left",
  anatomical = FALSE
)
#> <mesh_space> (v1)
#> • vertex space: "fsaverage5"
#> • hemisphere: "left"
#> • not anatomical, no MNI305 mapping
#> • units: "mm"
